result.title: SPELUNKA: A Framework for Finding Unanticipated Associations in Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are the backbone of many state-of-the-art multimodal systems, but often encode spurious and harmful associations from their training data. While prior work focuses on removing known biases from VLMs, methods for discovering unanticipated associations for retrieval tasks remain underexplored. We introduce SPELUNKA, an automated, inference-time framework for finding unanticipated distributional biases for retrieval tasks in VLMs without pre-specified labeled subgroups, inference-time human supervision, or model fine-tuning. Given a concept of interest, SPELUNKA generates captions for related images, extracts relevant entities from captions, and selects semantically meaningful associations. A frequency-based detection rule then identifies spurious associations by measuring over- or under-representation of these attributes in a VLM's top-ranked outputs relative to their full dataset distribution. We evaluate SPELUNKA across four datasets, and find that it 1) successfully recovers both synthetic and naturally occurring spurious correlations, 2) achieves an average AUROC of 0.93 across four datasets in identifying images strongly associated with a query, and 3) outperforms baselines in finding features that are strongly associated with a given query.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SPELUNKA，一个推理期自动化框架：给定感兴趣概念后生成相关图像描述、抽取实体、筛出语义关联，再用基于频率的检测规则，通过属性在 VLM 排序输出中相对全数据集的过/欠表示来发现未预期的虚假关联，并在四个数据集上验证其能恢复合成与自然存在的相关性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「描述→实体抽取→统计排序输出中属性的过/欠表示」的探针思路，可能可供核查 VLM 内部是否保留并使用了特定视觉细节与实体关系，从而迁移为 LVR 中表示诊断与视觉证据筛选的工具线索；但论文本身面向检索偏差发现，与推理状态生成无直接关系，需人工核查。
